evaluations.label: A
errors: 'Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested' is invented; nothing about a heart shape appears in the transcript (it was an odd-shaped structure with a spongy cover).
UI designer is named 'UL Hazred'; the transcript says Abdul al-Hasred.

The Project Manager is given 'Provide meeting notes in shared folder' and 'Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity' as action items; the first is only the PM saying he takes notes, and the second was never assigned.

Assigns 'Develop banana-shaped spongy case design' to the Industrial Designer and 'Finalize UI design' to the UI designer as individual tasks; the PM asked them to work together on look and feel and UI.
Presents the plastic cover only as 'debated'; the UI designer argued against it but nothing is recorded as decided. The wheel is never stated as kept after the cost discussion.
Several timestamps do not line up with where the topics occur (for example 22:55 and 20:26 for next steps).
strengths: Has an explicit action items section grouped by role.
Captures the wheel cost (50x, 12 euro budget), the motion-sensor cost concern for the light, the banana and yellow decision, and left/right symmetry.
Notes the concern about buttons moving through a soft case.
weaknesses: Omits the voice recognition chip email completely.
Does not clearly record the decision to keep the wheel despite cost.
Contains an invented detail and a garbled name.
Action items are over-assigned and partly invented.
Weak on what is open versus decided, and has no recap of previous decisions.

evaluations.label: B
errors: Next steps assign the final banana-form design to the Industrial Designer and the layout to the UI designer; the transcript only asks them to work together on look and feel and UI design (mild over-assignment).
'Hard internal structure' is a slight embellishment of 'odd shaped with a spongy cover'.
strengths: Cleanly separates the recap of previous decisions, the component decisions, the voice recognition update, the banana direction and next steps.
States clearly what was decided (wheel retained despite 50x cost, standard battery, chip-on-print, banana in yellow, wheel on top and buttons on the side) and what was deferred (voice chip decision).
Correctly records the ranked priorities, the 12 euro limit, the plastic cover reconsideration, backlight activation and battery concern, and left/right symmetry.
weaknesses: Omits the idea of using the wheel push-down for an extra function.
Does not mention that the Project Manager will send further instructions by email.
Plastic cover change is framed as a decision more firmly than the transcript supports.

evaluations.label: C
errors: 'IS1001c remote control' is not in the transcript.
Backlit buttons 'that activate upon movement' are stated as a decision; the activation method was debated and not settled.
'Arched internal structure' is not supported by the transcript.
The plastic cover is described as rejected; the UI designer advised against it but no group decision was made.

The voice recognition suggestion is placed under the industrial design section and described as 'to potentially add command features later'; it was raised by the UI designer and left for later decision.
Action items are listed as '(none)' although the designers were asked to collaborate on the prototype and the PM said instructions would follow by email.
Speaker numbers and 'UIZ'/'ID' labels are inconsistent and some roles are mismatched.
strengths: Readable summary plus a topic outline with good coverage of the flow.
Includes an Unresolved Questions section covering the voice chip, motion sensor cost and spongy material versus button presses.
Records the wheel decision with its competitive rationale, and the banana, yellow and spongy decisions.
weaknesses: No action items despite clear next steps (only appears in the outline).
Anonymous speaker numbers make it hard to know who said what.
Duplicates content between the summary and the outline.
Several statements are stated as settled when they were not.

evaluations.label: D
errors: Lists a 'preview button' in the earlier concept; the transcript says previous channel button.
'The wheel could be pressed down to recall a channel' is not supported; the transcript says the push down could be used 'for the record'.
'The market presentation ... [12:10]' and some other timestamps are approximate.
The 'Action items' heading is empty even though next steps are described elsewhere.
strengths: Accurately captures the wheel cost (50x), the 12 euro limit, the voice chip email with no decision made, and the ranked priorities (look and feel, innovation, ease of use).
Honestly flags the left/right-handed concern as not resolved.
Records the banana choice with the yellow, company colour and wheel-on-top reasoning, and the next steps including email instructions and product evaluation.
Opens with a short summary and uses timestamps.
weaknesses: Empty action items section and no named owners for next tasks beyond the joint prototype work.
Little on the battery, standard components and chip beyond a single bullet.
Dense nested bullets make it somewhat harder to scan for decisions.

rationale: B is the most accurate and the clearest on decisions: it separates previous decisions, component decisions, the deferred voice chip, the banana direction and next steps, with only minor over-assignment of tasks. D is close in accuracy and completeness and is honest about unresolved points, but has a garbled 'preview button', an unsupported push-down use for the wheel and an empty action items heading. C reads well and lists open questions, but invents a product code, treats the backlight trigger and plastic cover as settled, and lists no action items. A has an explicit action items list, but it contains an invented 'heart-shaped core', a garbled UI designer name, over-assigned tasks, and it omits the voice chip and the wheel decision.
